release_id_same_day_replay_review.startup_behavior: The staged plist has RunAtLoad=true. A new daemon executes its first one-shot scheduler cycle immediately on entering the loop. At observed 10:49, the current minute is not a slot; 10:30 and 10:00 are the eligible recent fixed/hourly slots and both have persisted claims. First cycle therefore finds no unclaimed scheduled slot; next scheduled slot is 11:00.

code_evidence.evidence: At daemon startup last_minute is None, so first loop immediately calls the one-shot scheduler before the wait.
Passes the new release_id into due resolution; unknown current minute returns NO_DUE_SLOT.
Checks claim file before receipt identity filtering; release_id filters old receipts, but existing claims still block exact/catch-up slots.

Dispatch claim key is claims/{mode}/{business_date}/{slot}/dispatch.claim.json and carries no release_id; valid non-FAILED receipt keeps a dead claim from being replaced. Failed dispatch alone releases the claim.
Claim acquisition precedes workload execution; an existing claim returns CONCURRENCY_SKIPPED. Claim release occurs only after FAILED aggregate receipt.

current_same_day_ledger.0901_and_0915: Claims absent; latest failures are UPSTREAM_NOT_READY. At 10:49, both are outside the 59-minute catch-up window; 09:15 also has an opening-window cutoff at 09:19.

release_id_same_day_replay_review.release_id_effect: A new release_id intentionally treats prior-release FAILED receipts as a fresh identity for retry/backoff. This can permit a retry of a failed slot after normal due/catch-up gates. It does not replay observed completed slots because their claims persist. A completed receipt with a missing claim could be ignored by the new-identity due filter; no such same-day completed slot was present in the observed ledger.
